question: Can a minimal ESP-IDF candidate emit the exact BH1750/SCD40 raw telemetry contract needed for genuine 10-minute acquisition?

environment.esp_idf_version: v6.1, official espressif/idf:v6.1 Docker image (GitHub Ubuntu runner)

checks.github_ci: PASS: Actions #40421852619, 83/83 host/synthetic tests on Ubuntu and 83/83 on Windows; portable C test executed
checks.esp_idf_build: PASS: Actions #40421852576, idf.py --version = ESP-IDF v6.1; Project build complete; ESP32-S3 target; no device

failure_learning: Initial C host build rejected CRC ternary signedness under -Werror; changed to explicit branches.
Initial host test expected SCD40 datasheet's 0x7B for 0x01F4, but documented CRC-8 polynomial yields 0x33; test corrected and discrepancy documented.
limitations: The portable host C test alone does not prove device behavior; a separate real ESP-IDF compilation now passes.
CRC does not authenticate sensor identity, calibration or flashed binary.
Firmware has not been physically tested; timestamps and cadence unverified.
next_experiment: Operator independently reviews wiring and port, flashes the verified build or a separately hashed local ESP-IDF 6.1 build, acquires >=600 s genuine raw dual-sensor telemetry, checks host-to-bundle chain and obtains independent setup review under issue #8.
advance: Genuine reproducible independent physical capture and setup review; then controlled repeated trials.
reframe: If firmware cannot produce continuous provenance-reviewed captures, retain as software instrumentation candidate.
source_blob_sha256_status: Exact Git blobs in draft PR; compiled binary SHA-256 preserved in CI log but binary itself was not retained for download
